state_profile.voting_summary: Illinois offers 40 days of early voting and no-excuse mail voting, with mail postmarked by election day accepted for two weeks afterward. Polls close at 8 p.m. Eastern; early votes and mail on hand are released first, election day precincts report through the night, and late-arriving mail is added for two weeks, Chicago's count in particular keeps growing. Mail ran D+45 versus R+16 on election day where counties break out modes, so Illinois drifts bluer well after election night.
